definitions.explanation: A form of traditional Japanese puppet theater in which large, elaborately crafted puppets are manipulated by visible puppeteers, accompanied by a narrator (tayu) and shamisen music. Designated as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

examples.japanese: {大阪|おおさか}で{文楽|ぶんらく}を{観|み}た。
{文楽|ぶんらく}の{人形|にんぎょう}は{三人|さんにん}で{一体|いったい}を{操|あやつ}る。
examples.english: In Bunraku, three puppeteers operate a single puppet.

examples.japanese: {文楽|ぶんらく}は{歌舞伎|かぶき}と{並|なら}んで{日本|にほん}を{代表|だいひょう}する{伝統|でんとう}{芸能|げいのう}のひとつだ。
examples.english: Bunraku is one of Japan's representative traditional performing arts, alongside kabuki.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Bunraku originated in Osaka and is one of Japan's three major classical theater forms, along with {能|のう} (Noh) and {歌舞伎|かぶき} (Kabuki). It features large puppets (about 1.2-1.5 meters tall) operated by three puppeteers: the main puppeteer ({主遣|おもづか}い) handles the head and right hand, while two assistants control the left hand and feet. The {太夫|たゆう} (narrator) provides all dialogue and narration, accompanied by {三味線|しゃみせん}.

The name comes from {植村文楽軒|うえむらぶんらくけん}, who established a puppet theater in Osaka in the early 19th century. The {国立文楽劇場|こくりつぶんらくげきじょう} (National Bunraku Theatre) in Osaka is the art form's main venue.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {文楽|ぶんらく}{人形|にんぎょう}: Bunraku puppet
- {文楽|ぶんらく}{劇場|げきじょう}: Bunraku theater
- {文楽|ぶんらく}を{観|み}る: to watch Bunraku
- {人形浄瑠璃|にんぎょうじょうるり}: puppet joruri (formal name for Bunraku)
